question: Will the October 1, 2026 hearing on OpenAI's motion to dismiss Apple's trade-secrets suit go forward as scheduled?

calls.reasoning: Reference class (civil motion hearings in N.D. Cal. still on calendar ~10 days out, fully briefed, high-profile) would put this near 0.8 YES. But the already-resolved check overrides the base rate: a September 14, 2026 minute entry on the case docket continued the combined hearing on Filings 38, 49 and 59 from 10/1/2026 to 10/14/2026 at 9:00 AM before Judge Davila, and moved the Initial CMC to the same day. Confirmed by two current sources (PacerMonitor docket text quoting the minute entry; MacObserver reporting dated Sept 19-21). Most news still says 'October 1' because it predates the continuance, so index-level hits are stale, not contradictory. Residual YES mass covers both sources misreporting the docket and the court restoring an October 1 session in the remaining ten days. No market prices this.

calls.reasoning: The already-resolved check dominates the base rate. A 9/14/2026 minute entry (docket 145) before Judge Davila continued the combined hearing on Filings 38, 49 and 59 from 10/1/2026 to 10/14/2026 at 9:00 AM, and moved the Initial CMC to the same day, leaving only the joint CMC statement due 10/1. Two runs retrieved that entry's verbatim text independently via PacerMonitor; MacObserver (9/15) reports the same continuance from the same conference; and 9/18 docket filings track that order's noon-9/18 deadline. All surviving 'October 1' reporting predates 9/14. The unconditional rate for a noticed federal motion hearing going forward (~55-85%) does not apply once a continuance to a named later date is entered; courts rarely re-advance absent a party motion. Run 2's higher number rested on having only one secondary source and on Oct 14 falling on a Wednesday off Davila's Thursday law-and-motion calendar - a real but weak signal, since complex-case hearings are routinely specially set, and the paired 9:00/10:00 settings look deliberate. Residual YES is almost entirely the chance the docket read is wrong (no run reached PACER; CourtListener and Justia 403'd), and even there YES further requires Filing 59 to be argued on 10/1 rather than submitted on the papers.
calls.reconciliation: Central dispute was factual: whether the 10/1 hearing had already been continued. Runs 1 and 3 independently quote identical verbatim text from minute entry 145 (status conference 9/14/2026) continuing the Filings 38/49/59 hearing to 10/14/2026 at 9:00 AM, retrieved from PacerMonitor; Run 2 did not reach that source and rested on MacObserver alone, holding back 15-20% for a possibly garbled report. No web access on this run, so I could not open PACER myself; I resolved it on the convergence of three strands the runs supply: two independent near-primary retrievals with matching quoted text, contemporaneous secondary reporting one day after the conference, and 9/18 docket filings that respond to the same order's 12:00 PM 9/18 joint-statement deadline - a corroborator that a fabricated or conflated continuance would not generate. Run 2's Wednesday-calendar objection is factually correct (Oct 1 is a Thursday, Oct 14 a Wednesday, and Davila's standing civil motions calendar is Thursdays) but is weak against that weight: specially-set hearings in complex cases routinely fall off the standard day, and the entry's paired 9:00 hearing / 10:00 CMC settings read as deliberate. The conflation hypothesis (with the Oct 13 CMC vacated in July on reassignment from Judge DeMarchi) is possible but unsupported. Because no run reached PACER itself, I do not treat the continuance as certain and leave a few points of error mass, discounted further because even a wrong docket read leaves YES requiring argument on Filing 59 specifically on 10/1 rather than submission on the papers. I adopt Runs 1/3's conditional reference class over the unconditional one. No market prices this on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or any bookmaker any run checked.
